newsitem.title: USA: Digital, Packard Bell NEC cuts computer prices.
newsitem.headline: Digital, Packard Bell NEC cuts computer prices.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp. and the NEC Computer Systems Division of Packard Bell NEC Inc. Friday cut prices of their computers, in the latest salvo in an industry price war.
Digital cut prices by up to 19 percent for models using Intel Corp.'s Pentium and Pentium Pro chips throughout its Venturis and Celebris personal computer lines in the United States.
Digital said its desktop models will now cost 5 percent to 7 percent less than Compaq Computer Corp.'s and up to 18 percent below those from Hewlett-Packard Co.
The Maynard, Mass.-based company estimated U.S. street prices would start at $977 for entry-level Venturis models, and $2,078 for the Celebris GL models.
Intel Corp. makes the Pentium chip.
NEC cut prices on its three lines of Versa notebook computers by up to 20 percent.
The NEC Versa 2405 notebook computer will cost $1,499 at stores, down from $1,699 previously.

NEC Computer Systems is a division of Packard Bell NEC Inc., one of the largest computer companies in the world. Packard Bell NEC is based in Sacramento, Calif. NEC Corp. of Japan owns a stake in Packard Bell NEC.
Digital's stock fell $1.125 to $34.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
